newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani vegoil rates seen up next week.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani vegoil rates seen up next week.

text.p: Pakistani vegetable oil rates will gain in the next trading week on increased local demand and higher prices abroad, dealers said on Saturday.
Dealers said the demand would increase in the local market because of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan which started on Saturday.
Vegoil consumption increases because Pakistani Moslems use a lot of oil for the cooking of traditional food items used during the month of Ramadan.
"The prices in international market also have a rising trend as China and Pakistan will be the buyers this month," a dealer at Saulat Enterprises said.
Dealers said vegoil stocks rose to an estimated 218,000 tonnes last week from 208,500 tonnes the week before. RBD palm oil and palm olein stocks rose to 180,000 tonnes compared to 175,000 previously.
Soybean oil and Sunflower oil stocks remained steady at an estimated 20,000, while the Ghee Corp of Pakistan's (GCP) palm oil and palm olien stocks jumped to 18,000 tonnes from 13,500 tonnes.
Wawasan Courage is discharging about 25,273 tonnes of RBD Palm oil at the Karachi Port, while Bunga Selasih sailed off on January 7 after discharging an estimated 11,987 tonnes of palm oil.
Sielo-Di-Milona with an estimated 12,000 soybean oil is expected to arrive in the second week of January.
Wawasan Megah is loading palm oil at a Malaysian port for Pakistan, while Wawasan Murni will also load palm oil for in January.
